subject: ophthalmology
title: Phlyctenular Disease, Pterygium and Pinguecula

steps.tx: **Phlyctenular conjunctivitis** is delayed hypersensitivity nodule at limbus or conjunctiva in children reacting to staphylococcal or tuberculous antigens, giving focal redness, irritation and photophobia. Nodules may ulcerate and conjunctival lesions heal without scar while corneal lesions vascularise and scar. Source antigen review includes lid staph carriage and tuberculosis exposure by setting prevalence.
steps.say: Hypersensitivity nodule gives focal limbal inflammation in children characteristically by antigen reaction. Lid and tuberculosis sources give antigen review direction. Corneal involvement gives scar risk.

steps.tx: **Phlyctenular keratitis** extends nodule onto cornea with fascicular ulcer trailing vessels across limbus, photophobia prominent in children hiding eyes from light. Steroid responsiveness is high but infection exclusion precedes suppression, herpes and bacterial ulcer in differential. Antigen source treatment reduces recurrence beyond repeated steroid courses alone.
steps.say: Corneal extension gives trailing vessels with photophobia in childhood phlycten disease seriously. Infection exclusion gives steroid safety before suppression. Source treatment gives recurrence reduction.

steps.tx: **Pterygium** is fibrovascular conjunctival growth onto cornea from nasal limbus in ultraviolet exposed adults, elastotic degeneration with wing shaped fold whose apex advances toward visual axis. It induces astigmatism by flattening and threatens axis by growth or recurrence scarring. Excision with conjunctival autograft gives lowest recurrence standard in modern surgery teaching.
steps.say: Ultraviolet degeneration gives nasal wing growth onto cornea in adults characteristically by exposure. Astigmatism induction gives visual effect before axis invasion. Autograft excision gives recurrence standard.

vis.caption: Conjunctival growth patterns. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Pinguecula** is yellowish elastotic conjunctival nodule at limbus that never crosses onto cornea, separating it from pterygium by corneal invasion alone. It inflames as pingueculitis occasionally, otherwise observes without surgery for cosmesis only reluctantly. Apex on cornea is therefore one question diagnosis discriminator at slit lamp.
steps.say: Limbal nodule without corneal crossing together gives pinguecula separation from pterygium simply at slit lamp during clinic assessment in adults. Occasional inflammation gives treatment need in pingueculitis episodes. Observation gives usual care in quiet lesions.

steps.tx: Pterygium recurrence after bare sclera excision historically high, autograft and antimetabolite adjuncts reducing it by technique generation. Recurrent disease scars fornix and restricts motility in aggressive cases needing specialist reconstruction. **Primary prevention** ultraviolet protection in outdoor workers delays incidence more cheaply than recurrent surgery cycles.
steps.say: Graft technique together gives recurrence reduction across surgical generations in pterygium care standards for outdoor workers in sunny regions. Aggressive recurrence gives motility restriction risk after surgery. Ultraviolet protection gives primary prevention in populations.

steps.tx: Conjunctival intraepithelial neoplasia and squamous carcinoma mimic pterygium or chronic conjunctivitis in elderly sun damaged eyes, gelatinous limbal mass with feeder vessels needing excision biopsy. Any atypical, gelatinous or unilateral persistent limbal lesion therefore biopsies rather than routine pterygium scheduling. **Masquerade limbal mass** rule protects oncology timing in conjunctiva clinics.
steps.say: Gelatinous limbal mass gives neoplasia suspicion in elderly sun damaged eyes needing biopsy urgently. Feeder vessels give masquerade clue. Routine scheduling gives dangerous delay.

steps.tx: Phlyctenular disease versus pterygium age split helps conjunctiva triage substantially: childhood limbal nodule suggests hypersensitivity, adult nasal wing suggests ultraviolet degeneration, and elderly gelatinous mass suggests ocular surface neoplasia needing biopsy. The same limbus hosts three age defined diseases, a demographic pattern examinations test strongly. **Age plus morphology** reads limbal lesions before investigations in conjunctiva teaching.
steps.say: Age together with morphology gives limbal lesion reading before investigations in clinic triage simply. Child nodule gives hypersensitivity direction. Elderly gelatinous gives neoplasia direction.

steps.tx: Anchors organise limbal teaching by age and morphology: phlycten nodules hypersensitise children to lid or tuberculous antigens, pterygium crosses the limbus while pinguecula stops at it, and gelatinous masses in elderly eyes need neoplasia biopsy. Source treatment prevents phlycten recurrence while conjunctival autograft prevents pterygium recurrence after excision. **Corneal crossing** is the pinguecula exclusion test in one slit lamp look.
steps.say: Corneal crossing together gives pterygium confirmation while stopping at limbus gives pinguecula at slit lamp simply. Source treatment and graft choice give recurrence prevention in care. Age with morphology gives limbal reading.

cards.b: Delayed hypersensitivity to staphylococcal or tuberculous antigen in children; treat source plus suppression after infection exclusion.
Pterygium crosses limbus onto cornea; pinguecula never crosses. Autograft excision minimises recurrence.
Excision biopsy for ocular surface neoplasia, never routine pterygium scheduling.
